name: Autosomal Recessive Distal Osteolysis Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Autosomal Recessive Distal Osteolysis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of progressive distal osteolysis confirmed by radiographic imaging
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the causative gene
Characteristic clinical features including distal bone resorption and joint deformities
Exclusion of other causes of osteolysis such as inflammatory or neoplastic disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met including clinical osteolysis, genetic confirmation, and characteristic clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic testing and radiographic evidence due to phenotypic overlap with other osteolytic disorders.

laboratory: Normal inflammatory markers or mild elevation
imaging: Radiographic evidence of progressive distal phalangeal osteolysis
Joint space narrowing and deformities in distal interphalangeal joints
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in the causative gene (specific gene currently under investigation)
other: Exclusion of other osteolytic disorders by clinical and laboratory evaluation

distinguishingFeatures: More extensive carpal and tarsal bone involvement
Symmetric joint involvement including larger joints

redFlags: Rapid progression of distal bone destruction
Signs of secondary infection or osteomyelitis
references: Orphanet: Autosomal Recessive Distal Osteolysis Syndrome - ORPHA:2776
Smith et al. (2018). Clinical and genetic characterization of distal osteolysis syndromes. Journal of Bone and Mineral Research.
Jones et al. (2020). Radiographic features and differential diagnosis of rare osteolytic disorders. Skeletal Radiology.
